Patient returns today for routine thyroid management, reporting ongoing fatigue
and some weight gain since her last visit. She remains on Levothyroxine 50mcg
once daily and has been taking it consistently; the prescription was refilled
today with three refills, to continue indefinitely.

On examination she is comfortable and in no distress. Blood pressure is 130/73
mmHg with a heart rate of 63 and respirations of 14 per minute. Temperature is
98.5F, oxygen saturation 99% on room air. Weight is 67.4kg with a BMI of 28.5.
She denies any pain today.

Laboratory review shows a TSH of 2.00 mIU/L, which is within the normal
reference range, indicating adequate replacement on her current dose. Her
hypothyroidism is considered well controlled at this time.

We will continue Levothyroxine at the current dose and recheck thyroid function
before her next appointment. She is advised to return in 180 days, or sooner
should symptoms of over- or under-replacement develop.
